readmeExcerpt:
# pstack Lauren Tan's [pstack](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/tree/main/pstack) is an opinionated Cursor skill stack that improves agent outcomes. This is a port for Claude Code, Codex, Pi, GitHub Copilot, Muse, and other agent harnesses. It tracks upstream and also carries named policy forks, each declared in [`tools/forks.json`](tools/forks.json). Tell `poteto-mode` your goal and it will invoke the correct workflow for the task. It keeps your code concise, simple and verified. For concurrency bugs and invariants that tests cannot reach, `/create-formal-verification-skill` picks the riskiest property in your code, verifies it with a tool that fits, and leaves a project skill the next agent reruns. The separate [agent-formal-verify](https://github.com/michael-denyer/agent-formal-verify) plugin goes deeper on the method, with guided TLA+ model checking, Lean proofs, and Kani for Rust. ## Built for Claude Code This port translates upstream's Cursor skills for Claude Code before installation. [Upstream's Claude Code install](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/tree/c742dd6/harness/pstack/claude-code) asks agents to translate Cursor names at runtime, using extra tokens and relying on them to apply the mapping correctly. This port also adds a SessionStart hook that routes tasks to `poteto-mode`. ## Install
Claude Code Run in Claude Code 2.1.292 or later: ```text /plugin marketplace add michael-denyer/pstack-claude /plugin install pstack@pstack-claude ``` Claude Code leaves auto-update off for third-party marketplaces, so pstack stays on the version you installed. To turn it on, run `/plugin`, open the **Marketplaces** tab, select `pstack-claude`, and choose **Enable auto-update**. To update once by hand, run `claude plugin update pstack@pstack-claude`.
Codex Run in your terminal: ```shell codex plugin marketplace add michael-denyer/pstack-claude codex plugin add pstack@pstack-claude ```
Pi Run in your terminal: ```shell pi install git:github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude ``` The package loads the skills and the pstack Pi extension, which adds the subagent, question, and wake-up tools the skills use, plus `/loop` and the routing instruction. Invoke a skill with `/skill:`.
GitHub Copilot Run in your terminal: ```shell copilot plugin marketplace add michael-denyer/pstack-claude copilot plugin install pstack@pstack-claude ``` This installs pstack for the Copilot CLI and the GitHub Copilot app, which share `~/.copilot`. Start a new session afterwards. Copilot ships no default pstack models, so the first skill that needs one runs `setup-pstack` to pick from the models your account lists, and later sessions reuse that choice. The Copilot build is tested on Copilot CLI 1.0.87 through 1.0.92. On those versions the routing hook's context reaches the session alongside other plugins' session-start context. If a later version keeps only one plugin's context, `setup-pstack` offers a [standing instruction](plugins/pstack/skills/setup-pstack/copilot.md#wire-it-in) for `~/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md` instead. On 1.0.92, once the CLI caches its computer-use experiment assignment, `copilot -p` sessions list no plugin skills and a `skill` call returns "Skill not found". Interactive sessions, the hooks, and the agents are unaffected.
Muse Run in your terminal: ```shell git clone https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude cd pstack-claude muse plugins install ./plugins/pstack muse plugins approve pstack ``` The first command installs the native Muse plugin bundle. The second approves its `SessionStart` hook and agent definitions, which Muse runs only after approval. Start a new session afterwards. Invoke a skill with `/` (for example `/poteto-mode`), which Muse lists for each user-invocable skill.
Other harnesses OpenCode (the CLI and the desktop app), Gemini CLI, Prime Agent, and skills-only Codex installs read skills from `~/.agents/skills/`. Run in your terminal: ```shell git clone https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude cd pstack-claude mkdir -p ~/.agents/skills for s in plugins/pstack/skills/*/; do target=~/.agents/skills/"$(basename "$s")" test -e "$target" || test -L "$target" || ln -s "$(pwd)/$s" "$target" done ``` To update, run `git pull` in the clone, then run the `for` loop again to link skills added since the last run. These installs have no routing hook, so ask for `poteto-mode` by name or add a standing instruction to the harness's instruction file. See [shared installation](docs/reference.md#shared-skills-installation) for per-harness notes and uninstalling.
### Configure pstack routes tasks to `poteto-mode` automatically. At session start, a hook injects an instruction that points the agent at it: the plugin's hook on Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, and Muse, and the pstack extension on Pi. Codex runs the hook only after you trust it through `/hooks`, and Muse only after `muse plugins approve pstack`. Other harnesses have no hook. Run `setup-pstack` to turn automatic routing on or off, change model defaults, or set a reasoning effort per role (`arena runners: opus @xhigh, fable @max`). ## Getting started ```text Use poteto-mode to fix the search filter resetting when I change pages. ``` For a bug, it reproduces the failure, uses `how` and `why` to investigate, delegates the fix, then reruns the failing case. If the fix crosses a function boundary, it brings in `architect` before implementation. You receive the fix and the failing and passing evidence. [Other playbooks](plugins/pstack/skills/poteto-mode/SKILL.md#playbooks) cover planning, features, refactoring, performance issues, investigations, prototypes, PR maintenance, shipping, and longer projects. ## Details - [Skills and slash commands](docs/reference.md#slash-commands) - [Runtime setup](docs/reference.md#runtime-support) - [Models and dependencies](docs/reference.md#configuration-and-dependencies) - [Maintenance and port scope](docs/reference.md#maintenance) ## Data handling pstack has no server or telemetry. Anything its skills ask your agent to read, including session transcripts, goes to your model provider. Scripts run locally, and PR tools use your GitHub CLI login. ## Contributing Thanks for helping make this port better. Bug reports, documentation fixes, and runtime improvements are welcome. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the checks and where your change belongs. Report vulnerabilities privately as described in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). To support maintenance of this port, [buy the maintainer a coffee](https://buymeacoffee.com/codenyer). ## License This port, including its modifications and additions, is also [MIT-licensed](LICENSE), © 2026 Michael Denyer. Original pstack © 2026 Lauren Tan; imported cursor-team-kit and thermos skills © 2026 Cursor. See [LICENSE-cursor-team-kit](LICENSE-cursor-team-kit), [LICENSE-thermos](LICENSE-thermos), and [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md).

releases.body: The Codex worker example and the `sonnet` entry of the Pi `openai` and `openai-codex` tables move from `gpt-6-sol` to `gpt-6.1-sol`. GPT-6.1 Sol is the newer Sol and costs less than GPT-6 Sol, so no role has a reason to stay on the older model. `models.json` no longer names `gpt-6-sol`.

The Codex single-model example is `gpt-6.1-sol`, the model the Pi tables map `opus` to, and the Codex panel example is `gpt-6-astra`, `gpt-6.1-sol`, `gpt-6.1-terra`, `gpt-6-luna`. The worker example stays `gpt-6-sol`, the model the Pi tables map `sonnet` to.

The Codex panel example is `gpt-6-astra`, `gpt-6-sol`, `gpt-6.1-terra`, `gpt-6-luna`, so a ChatGPT panel has four models like the Claude panel. The Pi tables are unchanged, because Pi's model catalog does not list `gpt-6.1-terra`.

`bootstrap.ts` runs the calling script again in a new Bun process after it installs `commander`, as upstream's does. The port had dropped that step in 0.9.23, so the first run after each plugin update imported `commander` in the process that had just installed it. Bun did not find the new `node_modules`, and the run failed with `Cannot find package 'commander'` unless Bun's auto-install fetched the package from the registry. The failure reproduced on macOS and Windows 11 with Bun 1.4.4 under `bun --no-install`. `watch-pr/fresh-install.test.ts` runs each entry point that way from a copy of the scripts with no `node_modules`. [#326](https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude/issues/326), filed by @Thanaen, found the cause.

[backnotprop/pstack#14](https://github.com/backnotprop/pstack/issues/14), filed by @yasuyuki, reports a `/no-comments` run that marked a correct Cargo comment for deletion, one saying that profile settings come only from the workspace root. The same run ended when a second report was rejected, before any accepted edit landed. The comment-sicko prompt deletes a comment whenever it is unsure a keep clause applies, and it named no source to check a dependency's rule against.

The agent now takes a comment that states a rule of a dependency, platform, vendor, or protocol to that system's documentation or source code. A kill of such a comment cites the page or file that refutes the rule or shows it binds something else, and the report lists each one. When the agent cannot reach either, or what it reads leaves the rule unsettled, the comment stays as a `HOLD` that names the rule and where to check it. `/no-comments` leaves each such `HOLD` in place and reports it open, and it restores as a `HOLD` any kill of such a comment that lacks a refuting citation. pstack

Lauren Tan's pstack is an opinionated Cursor skill stack that improves agent outcomes. This is a port for Claude Code, Codex, Pi, GitHub Copilot, Muse, and other agent harnesses. It tracks upstream and also carries named policy forks, each declared in tools/forks.json.

Tell poteto-mode your goal and it will invoke the correct workflow for the task. It keeps your code concise, simple and verified.

For concurrency bugs and invariants that tests cannot reach, /create-formal-verification-skill picks the riskiest property in your code, verifies it with a tool that fits, and leaves a project skill the next agent reruns. The separate agent-formal-verify plugin goes deeper on the method, with guided TLA+ model checking, Lean proofs, and Kani for Rust.

Built for Claude Code

This port translates upstream's Cursor skills for Claude Code before installation. Upstream's Claude Code install asks agents to translate Cursor names at runtime, using extra tokens and relying on them to apply the mapping correctly. This port also adds a SessionStart hook that routes tasks to poteto-mode.

Install

Claude Code

Run in Claude Code 2.1.292 or later:

/plugin marketplace add michael-denyer/pstack-claude
/plugin install pstack@pstack-claude

Claude Code leaves auto-update off for third-party marketplaces, so pstack stays on the version you installed. To turn it on, run /plugin, open the Marketplaces tab, select pstack-claude, and choose Enable auto-update. To update once by hand, run claude plugin update pstack@pstack-claude.

Codex

Run in your terminal:

codex plugin marketplace add michael-denyer/pstack-claude
codex plugin add pstack@pstack-claude
Pi

Run in your terminal:

pi install git:github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude

The package loads the skills and the pstack Pi extension, which adds the subagent, question, and wake-up tools the skills use, plus /loop and the routing instruction. Invoke a skill with /skill:<name>.

GitHub Copilot

Run in your terminal:

copilot plugin marketplace add michael-denyer/pstack-claude
copilot plugin install pstack@pstack-claude

This installs pstack for the Copilot CLI and the GitHub Copilot app, which share ~/.copilot. Start a new session afterwards. Copilot ships no default pstack models, so the first skill that needs one runs setup-pstack to pick from the models your account lists, and later sessions reuse that choice.

The Copilot build is tested on Copilot CLI 1.0.87 through 1.0.92. On those versions the routing hook's context reaches the session alongside other plugins' session-start context. If a later version keeps only one plugin's context, setup-pstack offers a standing instruction for ~/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md instead. On 1.0.92, once the CLI caches its computer-use experiment assignment, copilot -p sessions list no plugin skills and a skill call returns "Skill not found". Interactive sessions, the hooks, and the agents are unaffected.

Muse

Run in your terminal:

git clone https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude
cd pstack-claude
muse plugins install ./plugins/pstack
muse plugins approve pstack

The first command installs the native Muse plugin bundle. The second approves its SessionStart hook and agent definitions, which Muse runs only after approval. Start a new session afterwards. Invoke a skill with /<name> (for example /poteto-mode), which Muse lists for each user-invocable skill.

Other harnesses

OpenCode (the CLI and the desktop app), Gemini CLI, Prime Agent, and skills-only Codex installs read skills from ~/.agents/skills/. Run in your terminal:

git clone https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude
cd pstack-claude
mkdir -p ~/.agents/skills
for s in plugins/pstack/skills/*/; do
  target=~/.agents/skills/"$(basename "$s")"
  test -e "$target" || test -L "$target" || ln -s "$(pwd)/$s" "$target"
done

To update, run git pull in the clone, then run the for loop again to link skills added since the last run. These installs have no routing hook, so ask for poteto-mode by name or add a standing instruction to the harness's instruction file. See shared installation for per-harness notes and uninstalling.

Configure

pstack routes tasks to poteto-mode automatically. At session start, a hook injects an instruction that points the agent at it: the plugin's hook on Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, and Muse, and the pstack extension on Pi. Codex runs the hook only after you trust it through /hooks, and Muse only after muse plugins approve pstack. Other harnesses have no hook.

Run setup-pstack to turn automatic routing on or off, change model defaults, or set a reasoning effort per role (arena runners: opus @xhigh, fable @max).

Getting started

Use poteto-mode to fix the search filter resetting when I change pages.

For a bug, it reproduces the failure, uses how and why to investigate, delegates the fix, then reruns the failing case. If the fix crosses a function boundary, it brings in architect before implementation. You receive the fix and the failing and passing evidence.

Other playbooks cover planning, features, refactoring, performance issues, investigations, prototypes, PR maintenance, shipping, and longer projects.

Details

  • Skills and slash commands
  • Runtime setup
  • Models and dependencies
  • Maintenance and port scope

Data handling

pstack has no server or telemetry. Anything its skills ask your agent to read, including session transcripts, goes to your model provider. Scripts run locally, and PR tools use your GitHub CLI login.

Contributing

Thanks for helping make this port better. Bug reports, documentation fixes, and runtime improvements are welcome. See CONTRIBUTING.md for the checks and where your change belongs. Report vulnerabilities privately as described in SECURITY.md.

To support maintenance of this port, buy the maintainer a coffee.

License

This port, including its modifications and additions, is also MIT-licensed, © 2026 Michael Denyer. Original pstack © 2026 Lauren Tan; imported cursor-team-kit and thermos skills © 2026 Cursor. See LICENSE-cursor-team-kit, LICENSE-thermos, and NOTICE.md.

aiSummary.oneLiner: An opinionated agent skill stack for Claude Code and Codex to improve autonomous workflows.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Pstack is a specialized plugin and skill stack designed to enhance the capabilities of AI coding harnesses like Claude Code and Codex. It ports rigorous, verified agent workflows originally designed for Cursor into other terminal-based AI environments. The tool manages named policy forks to enforce concise, simple, and secure coding practices during autonomous generation. By invoking specific workflows based on user goals, it significantly improves the reliability and outcome of agent-driven development tasks.
keyFeatures: Workflow translation: Ports Cursor-specific agent primitives to work seamlessly with Claude Code and Codex.
Policy management: Maintains named policy forks to enforce strict coding standards and behaviors.
Goal-oriented execution: Automatically invokes the correct operational workflow based on the stated task goal.
Code verification: Integrates strategies to ensure AI-generated code remains concise, simple, and secure.
Multi-harness support: Designed to operate across various agent environments including Pi and OpenCode.

useCases.description: Use named policy forks to ensure AI agents adhere to specific repository formatting and architectural rules.

useCases.title: Complex refactoring
useCases.description: Guide agents through rigorous workflows to safely refactor large sections of a codebase.

useCases.description: Standardize agent behaviors across different AI harnesses like Claude Code and Codex.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: This project is for developers and prompt engineers who actively use terminal-based AI coding assistants and want to enforce stricter, more reliable workflows. It requires familiarity with CLI agent tools.
